subject: social
title: Earn, Save, Spend
about: Where money comes from and where it goes: earning by working, spending, saving for a goal, keeping money safe in a piggy bank or a bank, choosing when you cannot buy both, and a simple budget. NC 1.E.1.1 (scarcity and choice), 1.E.1.2 and 1.E.1.3 (money, prices and how they change choices).
tip: Give him three jars labeled spend, save and give and let him sort his next few coins.

cards.q: Dad gets paid for fixing cars at his job. What is getting money for work called?
Zoe walks the neighbor's dog and gets two dollars. How did Zoe get the money?
cards.note: Kids can earn money by doing jobs too.

cards.q: Using your money to buy something is called...
cards.note: Once money is spent, it is gone.

cards.q: Ben wants a toy robot that costs ten dollars. He has two dollars. What can he do?
cards.note: Saving a little at a time adds up.

cards.q: Where can a kid keep coins safe at home?
cards.note: A piggy bank or a jar keeps your coins in one safe spot.

cards.q: Mia saves one dollar every week. After two weeks, how much has she saved?
cards.note: Saving a little each week makes the pile grow.

cards.q: Who works at a bank and helps people put money in or take it out?
cards.note: Money in a bank is still yours. You can take it out later.

cards.q: Sam has three dollars. A ball costs three dollars. A book costs three dollars. How many can he buy?
cards.note: There is only enough money for one, so Sam must choose.

cards.q: Ava can buy a ball or a book, but only one. She picks the ball. What does she give up?
cards.note: Every choice means letting something else go.

cards.q: A plan for how to spend and save your money is called a...
cards.note: A budget helps money last until the next payday.

cards.q: Leo's budget says save half and spend half. He gets ten dollars. How much does he save?
Kim saved for a long time and bought her bike with her own money. How might she feel?
cards.note: Reaching a saving goal feels great.

cards.q: Money a family gives a kid each week, often for doing chores, is called an...
cards.note: Families decide if and how a kid gets an allowance.

cards.q: Giving some of your money to help people in need is called...
cards.note: Donating money helps groups that feed or care for people.

cards.q: You get money for your birthday. What are three things you can do with it?
cards.note: Many families use three jars: spend, save and give.

cards.q: A red ball costs two dollars. A blue ball costs five dollars. Which costs less?
cards.note: Comparing prices helps you make a smart choice.

cards.q: The store puts toys on sale, so the prices go down. Will more or fewer people buy them?
cards.note: Lower prices make more people want to buy.
